Verify and batch windows of up to 16 rows: HIP builds default to 16, narrow builds unchanged

A pipelined group of a layer split is its own window, so 32 slots on four cards were four groups of 8 and nothing
larger could run. The window limit is now a build option (STRATA_WINDOW_MAX_T = auto | 8 | 16; auto is 16 for HIP,
8 for CUDA; SYCL and Metal never set it): include/strata/kernels/window_limits.hpp.

A window of up to 8 rows runs exactly the kernels it ran before (HIP gfx1201 window 8 against main: 3096 of 3097
kernels identical, the other a debug variant; CUDA sm_86 and sm_60: identical or renamed but for a few prefill kernels
NVVM compiles differently, with identical results). The code for 9 to 16 rows is only reached by a wider window:
- per-row arrays of the verifier, the expert source tables (128 / 256 entries) and the remote / peer expert tables follow
  the window; CPU expert jobs stay at 8 tokens (a 9..16-row group is two jobs over the same expert);
- the hyper-connection read is made in slices of 8 rows (its Q8_0 launch would otherwise skip rows);
- the grouped expert kernels run a second pass (SKIP template argument) instead of a 16-entry shared array (51 KB,
  over the 48 KB static limit of CUDA);
- resident_plan runs on 128 threads (up to 8 rows, as it was) or 256; MMVQ, bf16 GEMV, shared expert and MoE combine
  take 9..16 columns only in a wide build; the sm_60 packed path runs wide calls in passes of 8;
- STRATA_P4_TIMING and STRATA_P4_TRACE (include/strata/program/pipe_probe.hpp): opt-in timing and trace of the
  pipelined windows, off unless set.

Tests: src/core/window_limits_test.cpp (target window_limits_test). Real 16-row windows (--batch 64 on four stages,
--batch 16 --batch-groups 1) decode the tokens they decode alone.

Residency-biased routing (STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR) is off by default again on 12 GB NVIDIA cards (#4402)

0.2.7 turned STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.5 on by itself on a discrete NVIDIA card of 13 GiB or less. Reports and our own 0.2.7 agent check (4.5 of 10
tasks with it on, 5.6 with it off) tie it to repetition loops and weaker results in long agent sessions, so the owner took the default back
(2026-10-29). With nothing set the engine now routes exactly as 0.2.6 and as STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0 did; STRATA_DEFAULTS=026 is unchanged.

- sm120_series.hpp: route_prior_default() answers 0 on every card; route_prior_resolve() is the pure rule the engine reads (a set value wins on every
  card); kRoutePriorSmallCard stays the 1.5 opt-in value.
- verify.cpp: g_route_prior() uses it; the "on by default on this card" start line is gone.
- Expert settings / Terminal: "Faster answers on 12 GB NVIDIA cards" is now an Off-by-default row that writes STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.5; the words
  say it is faster on 12 GB cards but can repeat itself in long agent sessions (nine languages). A 0.2.7 file with STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0 reads as Off.
- Tests: arch_defaults_test (default table over 12 cards x hip x integrated x 026, explicit opt-in values), speed-switches.test.mjs and
  tests/terminal/test_speed_switches.py.
- docs/DETAILS.md: both places that described the 0.2.7 default.

Qwen: the automatic expert cache leaves the reserve it was asked to keep - the ~245 MiB the load allocates after it are priced (#4474)

--expert-cache auto sized the cache from the VRAM free after the weights, less --vram-reserve-mib, the draft head and the other priced
buffers. What the load allocates after the cache and no setting prices - the CUDA libraries the prompt path and the verifier warm up
(cuBLAS handles and workspaces, lazily loaded modules) and the verifier's small buffers - came out of the reserve, so the card ended
about 240 MiB under it: 459 MiB free at --vram-reserve-mib 700 on an RTX A4000 16 GB, 457 MiB on an RTX A6000 48 GB, under the 512 MiB line
the serve check warns about at every request (#2065). Measured with STRATA_TRACE=1: -164 MiB at the prompt path and -80 MiB at the verifier
beyond the draft head, the same with --prefill 512, 2048 and auto, on both cards, and the same on v0.2.6 (so not new in 0.2.7).

auto_cache_slots() (include/strata/core/auto_cache.hpp, tested in src/core/auto_cache_test.cpp) now leaves kLateAllocMib = 256 for it,
unless the card could not keep min_slots (#496) after it, and not under STRATA_DEFAULTS=026. An explicit --expert-cache N and
--vram-reserve-mib N are untouched; the cache is ~100 slots (about 1.8% on a 16 GB card) smaller.

DeepSeek engine: a layer split's chunked prompt no longer deadlocks - the host waits for another group's flag before it queues the device-side wait (2x H100, IST-DAS-2.25bpw)

On a two-GPU layer split, every prompt on the chunked path stalled: a device's wait kernel spun for a
hand-off while that device's thread blocked in its first cuBLAS call, and the other device's thread too.
host_wait_at_least polls the same host-mapped flag (the kernels' signed flag - seq test) before the four
cross-group waits of the chunk path, so the kernel finds the flag up. The GPU work and its order do not
change.

engine: wait up to 20 s for the RAM the expert arena needs, then load with a plainer warning (#4051)

An arena load with 10 GiB available for a 40 GiB arena sent a 60 GiB host into
memory reclaim until it was reset.  The check that is there warns only (a
cgroup limit below the arena still stops the start), and its own example is an
engine that is still exiting.  Before the warning, the load now waits for the
RAM to come back, re-reading it every 0.25 s for up to 20 s, and says so in the
log every 5 s (STRATA_ARENA_RAM_WAIT_S changes the seconds, 0 loads at once).
If it is still short the load goes on as before, with the numbers; below half
of the arena the warning says the whole PC can stall in reclaim and names a
systemd MemoryHigh= as the way to keep one program from taking all the RAM.
Nothing is refused or capped.

detail::wait_for_ram is the loop with its sampler and sleeper passed in, tested
in file_expert_source_test (test_wait_for_ram).  expert_source.cpp passes
g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only against the CUDA 13.1 headers; the engine itself
was not built or run for this change.

Qwen: the PLE residency policy gives its lock back when the lock is what leaves the automatic conversation cache too little RAM (#4518)

The 0.2.7 policy locks the 26.8 GiB PLE table in RAM at start when table + expert arena + 8 GiB fit. What the rest of the load takes
afterwards (KV pools, pinned staging, host buffers of two GPUs) is not known then: on a 128 GB two-GPU PC it left under 5 GiB and the
automatic conversation cache turned itself off, a regression against 0.2.6, which kept 8192 MiB.

When the cache is automatic and the lock came from the policy (not --ple-io ram), the cache is sized first: if unlocking the table
would give the cache more room, PleTable::unlock() hands the lock back (the pages stay cached, the OS may reclaim them), the log says
so, and the cache is sized from the RAM then free. --conversation-cache-mib N and an explicit --ple-io ram are untouched.
ple_lock_blocks_cache() is the decision, unit-tested in src/core/ple_residency_test.cpp.

DeepSeek engine: slot_load() writes each tensor-parallel member's window ring and compressor group under its own device (#4350)

slot_load() selected the lead layer's device once and then copied into every member of a tensor-parallel group; the members' buffers
sit on their own GPUs, so on two identical cards (tp 2) the second member's copy ran with the wrong device current. A failed copy
makes slot_load() fail, and slot_take() then deletes the saved conversation. Every other per-member loop (restore, reset) already
selects the member's device; slot_load() now does too.

Conversation cache: parking an idle --batch slot no longer drops the main session's copy with the shared-prefix checkpoint (#4420)

A batch slot's chain holds one checkpoint (the one its admission copied in). park_slot() went through park_source(), whose
drop_superseded() (#342) removes a parked entry when the outgoing chain holds that entry's deepest checkpoint; the main session's
copy of the same conversation qualifies, and the root checkpoint at the end of an agent's system prompt went with it. The next
overlapping request then read the whole 5 K-token prefix again (323 ms in 0.2.6, 4130 ms in 0.2.7).

ConversationCache::supersedes_richer() says when the park would drop an entry that has a checkpoint the slot's chain lacks; park_slot()
then leaves the slot unparked (it is overwritten, as in 0.2.6) and says so. A slot with no such parked copy is parked as before.
The predicate and its test come from the report (shenmintao, #4420).

DeepSeek engine: the auto RAM store no longer reads a discrete GPU's pinned buffers as unified memory (#4147)

store_gb_now() took any drop of 4 GB or more in the free RAM between the first estimate and the end of the weight upload for a
GPU that shares the PC's RAM, and subtracted a context-sized reserve (27 GB at 256K). On a discrete pair (2 x RTX 3090) the
pinned staging buffers and the page cache cause the same drop, so a 256K context shrank the store from 48 GB to 15-18 GB and
decode fell from 9-12 to 3-4 tokens a second (a regression since 0.2.4.2).

The decision is now store_gpu_shares_ram() (ds4_experts_rule.hpp): the RAM must have dropped AND a device must report
cudaDevAttrIntegrated. Strix Halo, the DGX Spark's GB10 and the Apple path keep the old rule; a discrete card never counts.
Unit test in tests/dsv41/experts_rule_test.cpp.

Say plainly why a CPU without AVX-512 stops the engine: the pack folder without native_experts.txt, not the CPU, is the cause; doctor warns before the start, the launcher gives the next step, the SYCL engine names the folder like the CUDA one does

DS4_FAT_ROWS follow-up to the port: launches through strata_ds4_launch (the Mac build), off on Metal, only for the types f16_rows decodes (no trellis, no Q5_K / Q6_K down: a request would have stopped on 'not decoded'), at least 17 rows (the light kernels own the small experts)

DeepSeek engine opt-in: the busy experts of a prompt take FP16 GEMMs, not the tiles (DS4_FAT_ROWS=N, default 0: byte-identical path, the packed tiles run exactly as before).  An expert of N rows or more has its weights decoded to FP16 once (iq::f16_rows, the values the tiles multiply), the rows gathered (gather_f16), cublasGemmEx, clamped SwiGLU in FP16 (swiglu_f16); SetArgs skip_ge leaves those experts out of the tiles.  The tiles decode an expert's weights again for every 64 of its rows; a popular expert of a long chunk has hundreds.  Measured on the RTX 5090 with the IST-DAS 2.25 bpw pack, v0.2.7 base, DS4_FAT_ROWS=64: a 13K-token prompt 1,400 -> 1,950 tok/s, a 5.4K prompt 1,065 -> 1,181, decode unchanged (28-33 short, 47-49 warm).  3x V100, Maya-XS: +6-8% on 8K and 32K prompts.  The same products, the sums' order differs: greedy output can diverge after the first rounding (wording equivalent); KL vs the reference 0.276, the stock path 0.285 (the same band, measured on Maya-XS; not yet re-measured on this base).

sm_121 (GB10, DGX Spark) speed defaults and the fused prompt tile

nv_defaults.cpp gets an sm_121 table beside sm_86 and sm_60: STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 (fused IQ prompt kernels), STRATA_PREFILL_NVFP4=w4a4
(NVFP4 prompt MMQ with FP4 activations), STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1 (fused hyper-connection read), STRATA_SPEC_COST=1 (cost-aware MTP window).
Measured on one GB10 with paired A/Bs (docs/DGX_SPARK_LINUX.md); a switch the user set is kept. STRATA_SM121_PERF=0 turns the table
off, and so does the 0.2.7 master switch STRATA_DEFAULTS=026. Unlike the sm_86 / sm_60 tables these are not bit-exact (the fused prompt
path and the FP4 activations round differently; 24 of 24 greedy answers were identical), so the start line does not call them exact.

moe_fused_iq.cu: on a GB10 the work-item rule never reached its 128-row tile (the launch average is above 112 rows an expert at every
prompt size), so pick_ww takes the 128-row tile from 65,536 routed rows a launch up (+3% prompt at 16K and 32K; 4K keeps 64).
STRATA_PF_TILE_DEBUG=1 prints the choice. Other parts take the line they took before.

DeepSeek engine on an integrated NVIDIA GPU (DGX Spark): arm64 build and placement from MemAvailable

- ds4_gg_cpu.cpp: amd_family() on a non-x86 CPU read no variable the rest of the function uses; it now reports no AMD family
- exl3_cpu.cpp: kGemmK moved above the AVX-512 section, as exl3_cpu_gemm_scratch() sizes by it on every CPU
- ds4_model.cu: uma_free(): on an integrated NVIDIA GPU on Linux cudaMemGetInfo counts only MemFree, while the model files' page cache
  holds most of what the kernel can still give back. The placement, the CPU-lane warm-up and the vision tower size their room from
  MemAvailable less DS4_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB (default 6) when that is larger. A discrete GPU, HIP and Windows are not touched.
  On a GB10: 12,163-12,226 of 15,744 experts in graphics memory where cudaMemGetInfo's free placed 11,961.

Engine for the DGX Spark: the arm64 CUDA build on top of #3622

#3622 made the strata target compile on aarch64. This adds what a Spark build needs beyond that:
- the trellis dispatcher (tq_cpu.cpp, its scalar rows) is part of the arm64 kernel library, as it is in the Metal build, so the
  DeepSeek engine's CPU lane links; ds4_tq_cpu.cpp names the AVX units on x86-64 only
- a STRATA_PORTABLE build on arm64 sets ggml-cpu's -march to armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16+i8mm (STRATA_ARM64_ARCH) instead of the build
  host's; GGML_NATIVE OFF alone would leave plain armv8-a and no NEON dot products
- the x86 kernels' parity programs and benches are not configured on arm64; the test suite defaults off there (-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON
  still builds what builds)
- spark/build_engine.sh: the reproducible build of strata, strata-dsv41 and the picture reader into an engine folder, with the CUDA
  libraries beside them (RUNPATH $ORIGIN)

Every change is behind STRATA_CPU_X86 being OFF or inside a new file; the x86 and Metal builds do not take it.

Merge f-dsv41-mac (DeepSeek on Metal) into v0.2.7

The 0.2.7 DeepSeek changes (persistent-grid IQ kernels, int8 rounding batches, hc_mix_split with a block counter, head columns,
chunk-path knobs) are kept; the Metal engine's hooks sit on top of them: every kernel launch is strata_ds4_launch(), the rounding
batch ends in the Metal multi-quantiser dispatch, the head stays at 4 columns a pass on Metal (8 moves the KL), and the macOS
parallel expert prefetch is macOS-only.

native experts: the window-invariant reference rows are used only where they match the linked ggml dot (#3416)

native_arithmetic_parity failed on an Intel i9-13900K (AVX2 + AVX-VNNI, ggml built native)
in five of its eight configurations: "gu=16 down=20 ff=96 nt=2 token=0". Not the VNNI row
path: STRATA_NO_AVXVNNI=1 changes nothing, STRATA_NO_IQ4NL=1 passes. The IQ4_NL down
reference (iq4nl_reference_rows) differs from that ggml's one-token dot on the scalar tail
block of a row with an odd number of blocks (ff=96 is three): that ggml does not contract
`sumf += d * sumi` into an FMA, the reference lets the compiler do it. On the other
machines tested the two agree, so it is a property of the ggml build, not of the CPU.
With an unfused tail in the reference all eight configurations pass on that machine.

The invariant path now checks each reference once against the linked ggml-cpu on synthetic
blocks before using it (iq4nl_reference_ok for IQ4_NL with 2, 3, 5 and 20 blocks;
iq512_reference_ok for types 18, 21 and 22 with SwiGLU, on AVX-512 CPUs). On a mismatch
it prints one line and the invariant path uses ggml's own one-token dot per token: slower
on such a build, never different. The Default path is not touched; only the opt-in
STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1 decode reaches this code.

Tests: native_arithmetic_parity, eight configurations, on the i9-13900K (4,866,048
comparisons, with the fallback line), z440 and the owner PC (see the series notes).
